title: Descent to a finite coefficient field; $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ as a $2$-colimit
statement:
The coefficient ring $\Qlb$ is a filtered union of the fields $E$, but integral lattices exist
only over a single $E$. We therefore show that every object and every morphism of
$\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is defined over some finite $E$. For $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ and a finite
extension $F/E$ we write $C_F=F_X\otimes_{E_X}C$ and $C_{\Qlb}=\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}C$ for the
extensions of scalars, given by functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)$ and
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)$; since $F_X$ and $\QbarX$ are flat over
$E_X$ ([lem-sfb-subfield-flat], [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]), these need no deriving.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme.

1. Every lisse $\QbarX$-module is isomorphic to $L_{\Qlb}$ for a lisse $E_X$-module $L$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
2. For $C,D\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and every integer $r$, extension of scalars induces an isomorphism
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)}(C_F,D_F[r])\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
   \Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)}(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r]),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.
3. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

4. For rational coefficients $\Dctf=\Dbc$; these are the bounded constructible categories
   $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. By (2) with $r=0$ and (3), extension
   of scalars identifies
   $$
   \Dctf(X,\Qlb)\simeq\mathop{\text{2-colim}}_{E\subset\Qlb}\Dctf(X,E)
   $$
   as ordinary categories (in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]): every object of
   $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some finite $E$ and some $K\in\Dctf(X,E)$, and
   for $K,L\in\Dctf(X,E)$ extension of scalars induces a bijection
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{\Dctf(X,F)}(K_F,L_F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Hom_{\Dctf(X,\Qlb)}(K_{\Qlb},L_{\Qlb}),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.

proof.text: The standing setting makes the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ separated and of finite type. Finite type includes quasi-compactness. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine and hence qcqs. The diagonal of $f$ is a closed immersion; over each affine open its inverse image is an affine $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, hence quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-separated by definition. Applying permanence (2) to $f$ and the qcqs base proves that $X$ is qcqs. This verifies the hypothesis of lisse descent without using any Noetherianity assertion.

For finite $E\le F$, the two flatness statements say that $F_X\otimes_{E_X}-$ and $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}-$ preserve finite limits. The source and target here are the abelian module categories underlying the cited derived categories, so finite colimits exist. Clause (2) of the current change-of-scalars statement therefore makes extension of scalars right exact, and these functors are exact. The exact-functor clause of the derived-categories statement identifies their left derived functors with their termwise functors. Consequently the scalar extensions in the item need no deriving, including on the unbounded ambient derived categories.

source.place: opening paragraph (flatness and the definitions of C_F and C_{Q̄})

proof.text: By the preceding qcqs verification, part (1) of the existing lisse descent lemma applies to $X$. For every lisse $\QbarX$-module $L$ it gives a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a lisse $E_X$-module $L_E$, and $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E\cong L$, proving assertion (1).

Apply part (3) of the existing derived-Hom descent statement to the given $C,D\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and the given integer $r$. Its map $\varinjlim_{F\supseteq E}\operatorname{Hom}(C_F,D_F[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r])$ is bijective, which is assertion (2). This is an isomorphism of groups because the canonical scalar-extension maps are additive. The index is the finite subextensions of the fixed $\Qlb$ containing $E$, including $E$ itself, and the cited statement is natural for their transition maps.

Apply the current bounded-object descent statement in its explicitly specified coefficient categories: $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology over the pulled-back condensed ring $\Lambda_X$, inside the unbounded derived category of sheaf module objects. All finite fields are subfields of the fixed $\Qlb$, and scalar extension is the same derived coefficient change identified in Steps 2 and 7–9. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ the statement gives a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ with $(K_E)_{\Qlb}\cong K$, precisely assertion (3). For every finite $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Qlb$, it also gives $(K_E)_F\in D^b_c(X,F)$ and $((K_E)_F)_{\Qlb}\cong K$, justifying the common coefficient fields used below.

For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, the coefficient-heart statement gives $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)=D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$. The bounded-constructible definition identifies these with $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$, full subcategories of the ordinary module-derived categories; their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets. Thus assertion (3) gives the object clause in assertion (4), and assertion (2) at $r=0$ gives its displayed Hom-set bijection, with exactly the same scalar-extension maps.

Fix the coefficient-module conventions: $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ means module objects in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, with $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$, and $D$ is unbounded. The definition of $T_{E,\Qlb}$ explicitly identifies it with coefficient change along $\underline E\to\underline{\Qlb}$; these are precisely the layer-B categories and scalar extensions of Step 2. Thus the two derived extension definitions give the ambient $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$ with the intended pulled-back condensed coefficients, rather than discrete constant coefficient sheaves.

proof.text: Both ambient extensions preserve bounded constructibility by the two cited preservation statements. Restricting them to the full subcategories $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ and $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ gives exactly the functors specified in the two constructible-extension definitions. Their morphisms are the ambient derived morphisms by the definitions of those full subcategories.

source.place: final cocone paragraph, restriction to bounded constructibles

proof.text:
Choose the canonical tensor comparisons supplied by the scalar-tower coherence lemma for $E_X\to F_X\to\QbarX$. Exactness is Step 2; thus its derived clause gives $\theta_{E,F}:\Phi_F T_{E,F}\cong\Phi_E$, where $\Phi_E=T_{E,\Qlb}$. Restrict using Step 8. These are the transitivity isomorphisms of the ambient and restricted definitions: the comparison of the derived transitivity definition is, termwise, the unique isomorphism $\operatorname{Ext}_{F_X\to\QbarX}\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to F_X}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to\QbarX}$ carrying the composite adjunction unit $m\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to the unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, by the uniqueness clause of the conjugate-isomorphism lemma for the adjunctions of change-of-scalars clause (2) with the equal restrictions $\operatorname{Res}_{E_X\to F_X}\operatorname{Res}_{F_X\to\QbarX}=\operatorname{Res}_{E_X\to\QbarX}$. The tensor comparison sends $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $1\otimes m$, so it is that isomorphism. Hence they give the specified constructible cocone. For $E\subseteq H\subseteq F$, its additional comparison $\alpha:T_{H,F}T_{E,H}\cong T_{E,F}$ satisfies
$$\theta_{E,F,K}\circ\Phi_F(\alpha_K)=\theta_{E,H,K}\circ\theta_{H,F,T_{E,H}K}.$$
This is the cited lemma's derived tower equation for $E_X\to H_X\to F_X\to\QbarX$; all these extensions are exact by Step 2. In particular this equation is a cited theorem, not a consequence of the mere existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: proof (4), tensor transitivity coherence; final cocone paragraph

proof.text: The index is a set: its fields are intermediate subfields of the fixed $\Qlb$. The finite-subextension directed-set statement gives a finite compositum containing any two fields; fields containing a fixed $H$ again form a nonempty directed set. Their preorder category is small in a universe containing that set. Consequently the elementwise filtered-colimit lemma applies to the Hom-set colimits in assertion (2). The transition maps use the scalar comparisons of Step 9; its associativity and identity equations give their functor laws.

source.place: proof (4), common coefficient fields and the filtered Hom diagram

proof.text: Verify (Obj) for the cocone of Step 9. Given an object of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$, Steps 5–6 provide a finite $E$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ with $\Phi_EK$ isomorphic to that object. This is exactly (Obj) in the filtered-two-colimit definition.

For (Hom-surj), take $K_i\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_i)$ and $\varphi:\Phi_{E_1}K_1\to\Phi_{E_2}K_2$. Choose a common finite $H$ by Step 10. Put $A=T_{E_1,H}K_1$ and $B=T_{E_2,H}K_2$, still bounded constructible by Step 8, and
$$\varphi_H=\theta_{E_2,H,K_2}^{-1}\circ\varphi\circ\theta_{E_1,H,K_1}.$$
Steps 4 and 6 identify the target Hom set with its filtered finite-stage colimit. The representative clause (1) of the elementwise colimit lemma gives $F\supseteq H$ and $h:T_{H,F}A\to T_{H,F}B$ such that
$$\varphi_H=\theta_{H,F,B}\circ\Phi_F(h)\circ\theta_{H,F,A}^{-1}.$$
Here the domain and codomain are in the full constructible category by Step 8.

source.place: proof (4), finite-stage representative for a morphism

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_i:T_{H,F}T_{E_i,H}K_i\cong T_{E_i,F}K_i$ be the comparisons of Step 9 and set $g=\alpha_2\circ h\circ\alpha_1^{-1}$. Substitute the equation
$\theta_{E_i,F,K_i}\circ\Phi_F(\alpha_i)=\theta_{E_i,H,K_i}\circ\theta_{H,F,T_{E_i,H}K_i}$
from the cited coherence lemma into the preceding formula. Cancellation of inverse isomorphisms gives
$$\varphi=\theta_{E_2,F,K_2}\circ\Phi_F(g)\circ\theta_{E_1,F,K_1}^{-1}.$$
Thus the chosen $F,g$ satisfy exactly (Hom-surj).

source.place: proof (4), comparison equation for the transported morphism

proof.text: For (Hom-inj), let $g,g':x\to y$ in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,H)$ have equal images under $\Phi_H$. Injectivity of assertion (2) at $r=0$, established in Steps 4 and 6, makes their classes in the filtered Hom-set colimit equal; at the stage $H$ itself these classes are represented by $T_{H,H}(g),T_{H,H}(g')$, which correspond to $g,g'$ under the identity comparison $T_{H,H}\cong\mathrm{id}$ of the coherence lemma (Step 10), and the transition from $H$ to $F$ is $T_{H,F}$ conjugated by the comparisons of Step 9. Its index is small and filtered by Step 10. Clause (3) of the elementwise colimit lemma therefore gives a finite $F\supseteq H$ with $T_{H,F}(g)=T_{H,F}(g')$, precisely (Hom-inj). All three conditions now hold, so the definition gives assertion (4), with the object and same-field Hom descriptions already proved in Step 6.
